description: Each type's count is the number of behaviour-analysis records tied to its traders.

b.request: Count advanced-behaviour records for each trader type, including a separate group for missing types, using only exact matches from `advancedbehavior.translink` to `transactionrecord.transreg` and from `transactionrecord.trdref` to `trader.tradereg`; compute each type’s share of the total count and the unweighted average of those shares, then return the type, count, share, and share minus that average only for types whose share is strictly above it, without rounding or returning rows when the average is missing
b.sql: WITH type_counts AS (SELECT t.tradekind AS trader_type, COUNT(*) AS record_count FROM advancedbehavior AS ab JOIN transactionrecord AS tr ON ab.translink = tr.transreg JOIN trader AS t ON tr.trdref = t.tradereg GROUP BY t.tradekind), shares AS (SELECT trader_type, record_count, record_count::numeric / SUM(record_count) OVER () AS share FROM type_counts), compared AS (SELECT trader_type, record_count, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS average_share FROM shares) SELECT trader_type, record_count, share, share - average_share AS share_above_average FROM compared WHERE average_share IS NOT NULL AND share > average_share;

a.request: Link each advanced behaviour record to its transaction (`translink` = `transreg`) and then to that transaction's trader (`trdref` = `tradereg`). Use exact text matches and drop anything without a match. For each trader type (`tradekind`), with a missing type as its own group, count the behaviour records. Count every behaviour record, even when two of them point to the same transaction. Compute each type's share as its count divided by the total of the counts across all types. Which trader types have a share strictly above the plain average of the per-type shares? For each one, show the type, its count, its share, and its share minus the average share. Don't round anything, and return nothing if the average is missing.
a.sql: WITH type_counts AS (SELECT t.tradekind, COUNT(*) AS behavior_count FROM advancedbehavior AS a JOIN transactionrecord AS tr ON a.translink = tr.transreg JOIN trader AS t ON tr.trdref = t.tradereg GROUP BY t.tradekind), type_shares AS (SELECT tradekind, behavior_count, behavior_count::numeric / SUM(behavior_count) OVER () AS share FROM type_counts), compared AS (SELECT tradekind, behavior_count, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS average_share FROM type_shares) SELECT tradekind, behavior_count, share, share - average_share AS share_above_average FROM compared WHERE share > average_share

c.request: Taking the advanced behaviour analyses linked to their transaction (`translink` = `transreg`) and on to that transaction's trader (`trdref` = `tradereg`), using exact text matches and dropping anything that doesn't match: how much behaviour analysis does each trader type (`tradekind`) have? Treat a missing type as its own group. Compute each type's share as its count divided by the total of the counts across all types. Which trader types have a share strictly above the plain average of the per-type shares? For each one, show the type, its count, its share, and its share minus the average share. Don't round anything, and return nothing if the average is missing. Each type's count is the number of behaviour-analysis records tied to its traders.
c.sql: WITH type_counts AS (SELECT t.tradekind, COUNT(*) AS analysis_count FROM advancedbehavior AS ab JOIN transactionrecord AS tr ON ab.translink = tr.transreg JOIN trader AS t ON tr.trdref = t.tradereg GROUP BY t.tradekind), type_shares AS (SELECT tradekind, analysis_count, analysis_count::numeric / SUM(analysis_count) OVER () AS share FROM type_counts), compared AS (SELECT tradekind, analysis_count, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS average_share FROM type_shares) SELECT tradekind, analysis_count, share, share - average_share AS share_above_average FROM compared WHERE average_share IS NOT NULL AND share > average_share

d.request: Using exact text matches, link advanced behaviour-analysis records to transactions (`translink` = `transreg`) and then to traders (`trdref` = `tradereg`), dropping records without a match. For each trader type (`tradekind`), count the behaviour-analysis records tied to its traders, treating a missing type as its own group. Divide each type’s count by the total count across all types to get its share. Which types have a share strictly above the plain average of the per-type shares? Return each qualifying type, its count, its share, and its share minus that average. Do not round, and return nothing if the average is missing.
d.sql: WITH type_counts AS (SELECT t.tradekind, COUNT(*) AS record_count FROM advancedbehavior AS a JOIN transactionrecord AS tr ON a.translink = tr.transreg JOIN trader AS t ON tr.trdref = t.tradereg GROUP BY t.tradekind), shares AS (SELECT tradekind, record_count, record_count::numeric / SUM(record_count) OVER () AS share FROM type_counts), compared AS (SELECT tradekind, record_count, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS average_share FROM shares) SELECT tradekind, record_count, share, share - average_share AS share_above_average FROM compared WHERE share > average_share;
